Fucking typical.|[[Razz]]|sound=FNV_Razz RichBastardResort.ogg}} The '''House Resort''', known fully as the '''House Resort and Country Club''',[[:File:FNV House Resort sign 2.png|House Resort sign]] is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#New California Republic|unmarked location]] within [[Camp Golf]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Background== Before the [[Great War]], the House Resort and Country Club was one of the properties in the Las Vegas area owned by and named for [[Robert House]]. ===NCR military camp=== Managing to survive the nuclear apocalypse in remarkable condition, circa. [[Timeline#2277|2277]] when the [[New California Republic]] began their [[Mojave Campaign]] and moved into the region, the resort and its associated golf course were occupied and renamed "Camp Golf." During the [[First Battle of Hoover Dam]] against [[Caesar's Legion]] coming east across the [[Colorado River]], Camp Golf was on the frontlines and saw heavy action but ultimately continued to survive after the Legion's defeat. By [[Timeline#2281|2281]], due to the bulk of the NCR forces being moved to garrison the [[Hoover Dam]] for the impending [[Second Battle of Hoover Dam]], the resort has been left in the hands of the [[New California Republic Rangers]] led by [[Hanlon|Chief Hanlon]] as their regional HQ, serving as both a communications and quartermaster hub. However, the Rangers' occupying the resort has caused no small amount of tension between them and the [[NCR trooper (Fallout: New Vegas)|NCR trooper]]s that live in military tents out on the dilapidated golf course. ===Abandonment=== By [[Timeline|2296]], Camp Golf had been abandoned by the NCR forces once stationed there for unknown reasons, with a white flag planted at the entrance. Some equipment, such as armor and medications, were left behind in the retreat, though there were no signs of bloodshed. By that time, the [[Securitron]] [[Victor (Securitron)|Victor]], one of House's agents, had apparently been kept in the House Resort for over 10 years, and claimed to have suffered significant damage to its memories from modifications done by unknown persons, presumably the camp's former occupants.[[The Ghoul]]: ''"Victor? Is that you?"''
[[Victor (Securitron)|Victor]]: ''"V-V-Victor. That sure does sound familiar. Well, dagnabbit, spent the last ten years thinkin' I was a soda machine."''
The Ghoul: ''"What the fuck are you doing here?"''
Victor: ''"Well, b-b-beats me, pardner. Someone did a number on my numbers. Memory's all jimble-jambled."''
({{FOTV|2|3}}) Despite its abandonment, Victor claimed that the camp was still visited by Rangers "up in the hills."[[Victor (Securitron)|Victor]]: ''"Oh, you're leavin' already? Ain't nobody around to keep poor Victor company these days. Just them Rangers up in the hills."''
({{FOTV|2|3}}) That year, [[the Ghoul]] came to Camp Golf, apparently familiar with its status as an NCR military camp and seeking help from its garrison against Caesar's Legion, which was holding [[Lucy MacLean]] captive. Though the camp was empty, he encountered Victor inside the resort, who was seemingly deactivated but came back to life after his arrival. When asked by the Ghoul, Victor claimed to have no knowledge of where the NCR had gone. However, Victor was seemingly aware of developments in the region after the Second Battle of Hoover Dam, pointing to continued fighting between the NCR and the Legion as well as the Legion's ongoing succession crisis after [[Caesar]]'s death.[[The Ghoul]]: ''"Well, I gotta save a dipshit Vaultie from the Legion. Came here hopin' to get some help from the NCR."''
[[Victor (Securitron)|Victor]]: ''"N-N-N-NCR? I ain't seen 'em."''
The Ghoul: ''"Who's running these parts these days?"''
Victor: ''"Well you know how it is around here. The NCR and the Legion goin' at each other like cats and dogs. Though now, we got the Legion fightin' the Legion like cats and dogs, too."''
({{FOTV|2|3}}) The Ghoul would leave soon after, investigating Victor's talk of "Rangers up in the hills," which led him to a small group of holdouts led by [[Rodriguez|Captain Rodriguez]] near [[Primm]]. ==Layout== ===''Fallout: New Vegas''=== Situated north of [[Lake Las Vegas]], the exterior is very well preserved in the wasteland. Inside, there is a large lobby area with some small offices through a door at the rear, a storage area containing numerous [[Metal box (Fallout: New Vegas)|metal boxes]] and [[Ammunition box (Fallout: New Vegas)|ammunition boxes]] on the shelves to the left, a bunk area and kitchen to the right and two sets of stairs leading to a second floor with several bedrooms and an external deck. The house is potentially filled with about a dozen [[NCR Veteran Ranger|Veteran Rangers]] and half a dozen regular Rangers. ===''Fallout'' (TV series)=== What is shown of the resort's interior differs greatly from its portrayal in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. The little shown of the main lobby appears smaller, with display cases containing old artifacts. A connecting room, seemingly the same one as the barracks in ''New Vegas'', now has several work stations and furniture in the corners, rather than the rows of bunk beds used by the soldiers. Due to the NCR's abandonment of Camp Golf prior to 2296, the sole remaining resident inside the resort is Victor, who claims to have resided there for 10 years, since 2286. ==Notable loot== [[File:House Resort map.png|thumb|220px]] * Five [[Nuka-Cola Quartz (Fallout: New Vegas)|Nuka-Cola Quartz]] - Can be stolen from the shelves in the kitchen. * 22 [[Purified water (Fallout: New Vegas)|purified water]] bottles in the kitchen alongside a large amount of food. * [[Fallout: New Vegas keys#Lucky 38 VIP keycard|Lucky 38 VIP keycard]] - In Chief Hanlon's office. Used to enter Mr. House's secret chamber in the [[Lucky 38]]. * Three [[Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle cap]]s - On top of two dressers in a room upstairs. The room is the first in the right hallway, up the right staircase. * There are 25 [[Empty syringe (Fallout: New Vegas)|empty syringes]] in a room on the second floor, southern side spread all over the room on the bed, dresser and floor. * In the upstairs room just to the left of the collapsed northwest staircase, in the bathtub, are one oversized (1.04) scalpel just under the bonesaw, one undersized (0.98) scalpel just next to the same bonesaw and another undersized (0.97) scalpel on the surgical tray. Just across the hall opposite this room is a room with an inactive terminal and one oversized (1.06) scalpel on top of the surgical cart. [[Super mutant (TV series)|Super mutant]] (corpse) |robots =[[Eyebot (TV series)|Eyebot]] }} The '''Enclave research colony'''{{Ref|(Note)}} is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Built before the [[Great War]],"2076" is [[:File:FOTV Enclave research colony 05.png|shown]] on the wall while CX404 runs on the treadmill. the facility has managed to remain under the control of the [[Enclave]] by [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]] in spite of multiple failures and defeats suffered by the organization since the mid-23rd century. Enclave experiments seen in the facility include behavioral engineering (using selectively bred dogs in which sub-standard newborns are immediately incinerated), biological research (with captives held in a train car designed for handling live cargo), and energy production via [[nuclear fusion]].Events of {{FOTV|1|2}} The facility seems to be crucial to some form of overarching Enclave experiment intended to be tested on the surface, with the [[Vault]]s themselves supposedly secondary to whatever this experiment is.[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"I need you to tell me what you were really doing here."''
[[Hank MacLean]]: ''"And then?"''
Lucy: ''"And then I'm gonna turn you into the father I thought you were. You lied to me my whole life."''
Hank: ''"I know that's how you feel. You think this is the real world. The surface is the experiment. Not the Vaults."''
Lucy: ''"What experiment?"''
Hank: ''"I've already sent my R&D out into the wasteland. Their Boxes are the latest models, too. So you can't even see them. Unbeknownst to everyone, they're following orders written for them centuries ago."''
({{FOTV|2|8}}) The facility had a communications network which connected it to several [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] assets and facilities on the West Coast, including the [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]; a [[Las Vegas management Vault|management Vault]] built under [[Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]]; and [[Vault 33]] in [[Santa Monica]], California via a Pip-Boy kept by Enclave asset [[Hank MacLean]].{{FOTV|2|8}}: This Pip-Boy is seen inside Hank's keepsakes box, and Steph Harper uses it to contact the Enclave at this facility. Its communications infrastructure also seemingly allowed it to listen on many other radio frequencies used throughout the wasteland.[[Steph Harper]]: ''"This is Stephanie Harper. Hank MacLean's wife. I don't know how this works, exactly, but he said that you were always listening, and... If you can hear this... initiate Phase 2."''
({{FOTV|2|8}}){{FOTV|2|8}}: When the Enclave colony is shown and the messages from Hank and Norm are played, many other overlapping voices and messages, many of which are not directed to the Enclave or to anyone in particular, are heard. In 2296, the facility received word from [[Steph Harper]], the wife of Hank MacLean, to begin Phase Two of this experiment. It is unclear what specifically Phase Two entails, but it is suggested that it involves the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]] and the populations of some Vaults, including [[Vault 32|Vaults 32]] and 33.[[Ronnie McCurtry|Ronnie]]: ''"Hey, boss. Now that we've found food, it's time for phase two?"''
[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"What is your name?"''
Ronnie: ''"Oh, um, I'm Ronnie. McCurtry."''
Norm MacLean: ''"I decide the next steps up here, Ronnie."''
Ronnie: ''"I know, yeah, you're the-- you're the boss. I know you call the shots. Just thought I'd introduce myself, 'cause I was Bud's personal assistant."''
Norm MacLean: ''"Hm, so?"''
Ronnie: ''"So, uh, let's just say I was the guy who took the lunch orders when Bud was meeting with the Vault investors. 'Future Enterprise Ventures'? The whole plan for Vaults 32 and 33?"''
Norm MacLean: ''"What do you know about that?"''
Ronnie: ''"Like I said, I was just the guy who got the lunch orders, but I do know that Phase 2 was very important to the experiment."''
({{FOTV|2|4}}) {{Small|In "[[The Wrangler]]," "Future Enterprise Ventures" is explicitly confirmed to be a cryptonym of "Forced Evolutionary Virus," and these "investors" are confirmed by [[Robert House]] in "[[The Strip]]" to be the Enclave.}}{{FOTV|2|5}} ==In the TV series== ===[[The Target]]=== At an unspecified point in time, Enclave scientists study and measure the weight of newborn puppies bred in the facility, with the ones falling under the minimum 10 ounces being thrown into an incinerator. [[Siggi Wilzig]], one of the scientists, weighs a particular puppy designated [[CX404]] and seemingly has a change of heart upon seeing her, as he secretly alters the weight scale to show her meeting the minimum weight requirement and takes her on as his test subject. As he is leading her to his private lab, they stop as scientists pass by a [[Enclave soldier (TV series)|guard]] checkpoint wheeling a gurney with the corpse of a [[Super mutant (TV series)|super mutant]] on it. As time passes, Wilzig nurtures the growing CX404 in his lab in secret while working on a project involving a pre-War [[cold fusion]] device once owned by the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]. Sometime around 2296, as Wilzig prepares to leave the facility to bring the device to his benefactor [[Lee Moldaver]] in [[New California]], he and CX404 are discovered by an [[Enclave administrator|administrator]] who gets into a scuffle with Wilzig before pushing him away and activating an alarm, only to be mauled to death by the canine defending her master immediately after. Trying to make a quick escape, Wilzig and CX404 navigate through the facility and exit onto the exterior surface level. They are discovered by an automated turret that fires upon them as they flee from the facility but are able to get away unharmed. Despite its secretive nature, the facts of Wilzig's flight from the facility, his Enclave ties, the artifact he brought with him, and his destination are uncovered by members of the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth Brotherhood of Steel]]. They later issue the mission to locate Wilzig and recover the artifact to the [[Knights of San Fernando]], a Brotherhood chapter active in the [[Los Angeles]] area. ===[[The Strip]]=== [[Steph Harper]], cornered by angry [[Vault 32 dweller]]s after [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] revealed her to be a pre-War [[Canada|Canadian]], uses an Enclave Pip-Boy which Hank kept stored in his keepsake box to call the Enclave facility via an emergency frequency, telling them to begin Phase 2 of their experiment. These details are received by the Enclave facility, where several scientists and guards are seen walking around, along with a single [[Eyebot (TV series)|Eyebot]], in the atrium. Steph's message is shown being transcribed on a terminal labeled as Commstation 4, which registers the message as a request to initiate Phase 2. After this, a full exterior view of the facility is shown, revealing it to be a set of two buildings on either side of a gorge in a snowy, mountainous area, connected by several bridges. Many other communications are heard, including undirected requests for help, but also Hank MacLean's message from the Vault-Tec facility in Las Vegas (as heard in "The Innovator") and Norm's message from the Los Angeles Vault-Tec headquarters (as heard in "The Handoff,") revealing that the Enclave at the facility have been listening in on everyone. ==Layout== The exterior structure of the colony is a non-descript warehouse complex in an unspecified snowy, mountainous region. The building's most distinguishing feature is the large, glass-covered roof. Behind its walls, the majority of the facility is underground, with the surface portion merely the crown of a vast underground storage facility. Seemingly stretching across eight stories, the facility is built around a 200-meter-long atrium used for loading and unloading freight trains. Staggered loading balconies and a cargo crane remain present, although they have since been repurposed by the facility for research. ==Personnel== * [[Siggi Wilzig]] (formerly) * [[Enclave administrator]] * [[Enclave scientist (TV series)|Enclave scientists]] * [[Enclave soldier (TV series)|Enclave soldiers]] ==Appearances== The Enclave research colony appears {{in|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|2=102|16=208}} ==Behind the scenes== * {{Note|(Note)}} The name of the facility is never stated in the show's [[Fallout TV series season 1|first season]]. The title of this page is completely conjectural and intended to distinguish it from the [[Enclave research facility]] depicted {{In|FO76}}. * The location's atrium scenes were shot at the New York [[wikipedia:Brooklyn_Army_Terminal|Brooklyn Army Terminal]], warehouse B, dressed up with additional decals and cleaned up for filming. ==Gallery== FOTV Enclave research colony 01.png FOTV Enclave research colony 02.png FOTV Enclave research colony 03.png FOTV Enclave research colony 04.png FOTV Enclave research colony 05.png FOTV Enclave research colony 06.png FOTV Enclave research colony 07.png FOTV Enclave research colony 08.png FOTV Enclave research colony 09.png FOTV Enclave research colony 10.png FOTV Enclave research colony 11.png FOTV Enclave research colony 12.png FOTV Enclave research colony 13.png FOTV Enclave research colony 14.png FOTV Enclave research colony 15.png FOTV Enclave research colony 16.png FOTV Enclave research colony 17.png FOTV Enclave research colony 18.png FOTV Enclave research colony 19.png FOTV Enclave research colony 20.png FOTV Enclave research colony 21.png ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Enclave}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Enclave locations]] [[de:Enklave-Forschungskolonie]] [[ru:Исследовательская лаборатория Анклава]]

It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Background== ===Pre-War resort and NCR camp=== Prior to the [[Great War]], the main building was known as the [[House Resort]], with an accompanying golf course belonging to [[Robert House|Mr. House]]. Circa [[Timeline#2277|2277]] following the nuclear apocalypse, when the [[New California Republic]] began their [[Mojave Campaign]] and later came into conflict with [[Caesar's Legion]] from the east, the renamed "Camp Golf" was on the frontlines of the [[First Battle of Hoover Dam]]. This has caused no small amount of tension between the Rangers and troopers as the latter are forced to camp in military tents on the dilapidated golf course, while the former enjoy all the luxuries a pre-War resort provides. Additionally, owing to the camp's position far from the frontlines of the impending [[Second Battle of Hoover Dam]], it is considered a dumping ground for washouts and poor performers that no commander wants assigned to their garrison. Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series).original_wikitext:
{{for|the ''[[Fallout 4]]'' location|Vault-Tec Regional HQ|the mentioned-only ''[[Fallout 2]]'' location|Vault-Tec headquarters (Los Angeles)}} {{Infobox location |games =FOTV |label =Pre-War |image =FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Top.png |label2 =Post-War |image2 =FoTV Vault-Tec headquarters.png |part of =[[Boneyard|Los Angeles]] |factions = |owners =[[Ma June]] and [[Barv]] (2296) |pre-war =[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] }} The '''Vault-Tec headquarters''',[https://www.polygon.com/fallout-season-2-easter-egg-show ''Polygon'' - "Every Fallout Season 2 Easter Egg So Far"]: ''"Norm and his crew of vaulties make it to the Vault-Tec headquarters, and, as Norm is browsing one of the terminals, he learns a little about the Forced Evolutionary Virus (F.E.V.), which we know is what leads to the discovery of supermutants."''[https://www.pcgamer.com/movies-tv/fallout-season-2-episode-5-recap-another-player-at-the-table ''PC Gamer'' - "Fallout Season 2 Episode 5 recap: 'Another player at the table'"]: ''"Meanwhile, Norm and his crew of defrosted junior executives have made it to a Vault-Tec Headquarters, where they find the corpse of the receptionist, Janice."''[https://decider.com/2026/01/14/fallout-season-2-episode-5-recap ''Decide'' - "'Fallout' Season 2 Episode 5 Recap: What Happened in Vegas…"]: ''"Norm and his crew of thawed-out Vault-Tec managers make it to Vegas themselves, where they infiltrate the old Vault-Tec headquarters."'' also called the '''Vault-Tec building''',Referred to as such in the audio description of "The Beginning" is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Located in [[Los Angeles]] in southern [[State#California|California]], the building was one of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]'s headquarters and housed the offices of executives such as [[Barb Howard]] and [[Bud Askins]], who oversaw the company's Southern California operations.[[Bud Askins]]: ''"Mr. Howard, great work today."''
[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]: ''"Ah. Oh, thanks. Thanks, man."''
Bud Askins: ''"Bud Askins. I oversee our Southern California operations."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}) After the Great War, the building was left abandoned, with the corpses of pre-War employees still strewn about. In 2296, following the destruction of [[Filly]] by the [[Knights of San Fernando]], former Filly residents [[Ma June]] and [[Barv]] moved into the lobby of the Vault-Tec headquarters, claiming it as their new squat and [[Radroach (TV series)|radroach]] farm. ==Layout== The Vault-Tec building is a large skyscraper designed in a Mid-Century Modern architectural style, located somewhere within Los Angeles. There is a parking lot in front of the main entrance, leading into a lobby with elevators adjacent to the reception desk. A conference room was at the back of the ground floor. Elsewhere in the building, there were a set of adjoining communications rooms. Barb Howard's office was in another space nearby. There was also a room, presumably adjacent to Barb's office, that was used as a waiting room by Cooper Howard when he visited to spy on his wife. Some rooms on other floors of the building are also seen. One floor includes another conference room adjacent to a working area with several desks and cubicles and the elevator hall nearby; this was the area used by Barb Howard for her meeting with (the body double of) Robert House regarding cold fusion. In another unknown area, there was a large, two-story meeting room with seats on a ledge overlooking the main circular conference table, with a holographic map of the U.S. behind them; this space was used by Barb and Bud Askins to host a secret meeting about the Vault experiments. One hallway in some area of the building, seen in the credits sequence of "[[The Other Player]]," was shown to include multiple Vault-Tec research areas. There were rooms for "Vault-Tec Agriculture R&D," "Vault-Tec Toilet R&D," "Door Engineering," "Water Chip R&D," as well as "[[Forced Evolutionary Virus|F.E.V. Cultivation]]." One end of this hall included a security checkpoint, guarded by a [[sentry bot]], leading into the highly restricted-access Human Resources R&D Department. The other end attached to a standard office space, at the end of which was the office of Bud Askins. Askins decorated his office with numerous posters of Cooper Howard's movies, as well as a [[Giddyup Buttercup]], ''[[Grognak the Barbarian]]'' comics and a figurine, and a [[Brain bot|Rollerbrain]] user manual. After the Great War, the building's entrance and windows, as well as the door to an adjacent hallway, are seen to have been boarded up by 2296. The lobby was painted with graffiti in some places, calling out Vault-Tec for being "liars." Corpses of some of the building's employees were still present, including the receptionist [[Janice (TV series)|Janice]], as well as the janitor and two others who seemingly committed suicide using [[Plan D]] pills. By July 2296, the lobby had been claimed by Ma June and Barv after they fled Filly. They boarded up the elevators, which they were using to hold radroaches for farming, and set the first floor conference room as an armory. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The Beginning]]=== Sometime in the early-to-mid 2070s, Barb was driven to the headquarters by her then-husband [[Cooper Howard]], where they also encountered Bud as Barb entered the building. Unbeknownst to either of them, Cooper had secretly planted a listening device given to him by [[Lee Moldaver|Kate Williams]] into Barb's [[Pip-Boy 3000 Mark V|Pip-Boy]] in order to confirm his suspicions that Vault-Tec was up to something shady. However, he realizes just after Barb entered the HQ that the device had a limited range, forcing him to trick his way into the building by convincing Barb's secretary [[Betty Pearson]] that he wanted to wait in her office. Meanwhile, Bud and Barb go to a private section of the building, containing a secure boardroom where they begin a meeting with various corporate moguls representing big companies like [[REPCONN Aerospace]], [[West Tek]], [[Big MT (company)|Big MT]], and [[RobCo Industries]].[https://gamerant.com/fallout-tv-show-vault-tec-pre-war-design ''Gamerant'' - "Fallout TV Show's Production Designer Talks Making Vault-Tec From the Ground Up"]Events of {{FOTV|1|8}} Unaware of Cooper's listening in, Bud discusses with the moguls about the progression of Project Safehouse, Vault-Tec's joint operation with the [[United States government]] to construct a vast series of subterranean fallout shelters known as [[Vault]]s as a proactive defense against nuclear war and offers potential avenues of collaboration with their various groups. After the meeting descends into bickering over Vault-Tec's methods, Barb, seemingly taking cues from a private message from a [[man in shadows]] watching the meeting from an elevated section, takes the reins and formally offers each of the moguls a selection of the over 100 vaults in the country for their own use. While the others begin brainstorming ideas for experiments to perform on their populations of test subjects, [[Robert House]] questions how Vault-Tec plans to ensure that the Vaults are actually used. To Cooper's shock, Barb openly suggests that the corporations orchestrate the nuclear apocalypse themselves to guarantee that theirs will be the only monopoly left after the dust and fallout clears. Cooper is left stunned by the revelation of his wife's heartlessness, such that he does not initially react to being introduced to one of Bud's junior managers, [[Hank MacLean|Henry "Hank" MacLean]] who wanted to meet him due to his fandom for Cooper's acting work. ===[[The Wrangler]]=== Around July 2296, [[Norm MacLean]] and a group of [[Vault 31 dweller]]s are led to the Vault-Tec headquarters by [[Ronnie McCurtry]] to enact phase two of the [[Bud's Buds]] project plan. By that time, the headquarters had been left abandoned, with the remains of its former employees still strewn about. Part of the first floor had been claimed by [[Ma June]] and [[Barv]], former residents of the junk town of [[Filly]] who were forced to relocate due to the [[Knights of San Fernando]] having burned down their town, and partially turned it into a radroach farm. ===[[The Strip]]=== During a struggle, [[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]] inadvertently hits an elevator button, releasing a swarm of radroaches on the [[Vault 31 dweller]]s. Only Norm and an injured Claudia survive the attack and Norm takes Claudia away from the building in a cart. ==Notes== * A different [[Vault-Tec headquarters (Los Angeles)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] also in [[Los Angeles]] was mentioned in ''[[Fallout 2]]''. It is unclear whether these are meant to be the same location or separate ones, but the differences in these locations' appearances is intentional (see [[#Behind the scenes|below]]). * As seen in "The Beginning," the building is marked with signage for Vault-Tec Industries rather than the Vault-Tec Corporation. These two names have been used seemingly interchangeably for Vault-Tec throughout the ''Fallout'' series; the TV series has specifically only used "Vault-Tec Industries" so far. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quotation|The basement layer was based on Dr. Strangelove, the movie, with the light, roundtable, and cement room. It was fun to do. That was in the middle of Manhattan in a theater, so we had to use whatever we could to pull all that stuff together, because you know we shot in New York and also in Namibia and Utah, all to do LA.|[[Howard Cummings]]}} * For season 1, the exterior scenes of the Vault-Tec building were shot at [https://www.fordham.edu/graduate-school-of-social-service/about/campus-locations/westchester-campus/ Fordham University's Westchester Graduate School of Social Service], with the entire superstructure digitally added in post-processing. The site was chosen by Paul Kramer, a member of the film crew's location management team. It was selected due to its mid-century aesthetic, which the team wanted for pre-War Los Angeles; the structure of the building as seen in the TV series was based on the [[Vault-Tec Regional HQ]] found in [[Boston]] in ''[[Fallout 4]]'', but given a "West Coast architecture twist." ** According to [[Howard Cummings]], production designer on the TV series, it was intentional that the building was not a recreation of the "core LA Vault-Tec Headquarters" previously seen in ''Fallout 2'', due to his intention to have the pre-War scenes fit a "slicker" mid-century look. * The arrangement of the conference room is a deliberate reference to [https://pl.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plik:Dr._Strangelove_-_The_War_Room.png the war room] in the 1964 film ''Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb''. In the movie, the titular [[wikipedia:Dr._Strangelove|Dr. Merkwurdigliebe]] actually proposes the construction of nuclear shelters not dissimilar to Vaults in the event of Soviet nuclear aggression in the final act. Unlike the HQ building's exterior and suite shots, the conference scene was filmed in a Manhattan movie theater. ==Gallery== FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Top.png|Superstructure (all CGI) FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Ground Floor.png|Ground floor (dressed-up campus building) FOTV Vault-Tec Industries building.png|Composite image showing the entire building FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Suite 1.png|One of the suites in the building FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Suite 2.png FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Conference Room 1.png|The double-story conference room FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Conference Room 2.png FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Conference Room 3.png FOTV Vault-Tec Industries Building Conference Room 4.png FTV S2E6 Still 002.png FTV S2E6 Still 004.png FTV S2E6 Still 003.png ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Vault-Tec Corporation]]

Only at Mick and Ralph's!|[[Mick & Ralph's crier]]|''[[Fallout: New Vegas]]''|sound=FNV MRCrier AllowedToSell.ogg}} '''Mick & Ralph's''' is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Freeside|unmarked location]] within [[Freeside]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Background== Providing some of the finest quality trinkets to discerning customers, while serving the riff-raff the usual low-grade armaments, the owners maintain a thriving business even on the seedier side of Freeside with [[Mick (Fallout: New Vegas)|Mick]] selling [[Fallout: New Vegas weapons|weapons]] and [[Ralph (Fallout: New Vegas)|Ralph]] selling [[Fallout: New Vegas consumables|consumables]] and special services. ==Layout== Situated just inside of [[Freeside's east gate]], the area out front of the shop typically has [[Rotface]] seated against an adjacent building to the right, and [[Max (Fallout: New Vegas)|Max]] and [[Stacey]] running around in front during the day. When coming into the building, Ralph will be sitting on the right behind his desk. There are shelves on the wall to the right of where Mick is standing, and a central "shelf" made of washing machines in the middle of the room. To the right of Mick is a staircase that leads to a room upstairs that comprises Mick and Ralph's bedrooms and a few other items such as washing machines and desks. Ralph sleeps in the queen bed, while Mick sleeps in the single bed. A few skill magazines can be found on the second floor, including ''[[Tæles of Chivalrie]]'', ''[[Fixin' Things]]'', and ''[[Programmer's Digest]]''. [[File:Mick's_special_store.jpg|220px|thumb|Mick's special weapons hideout]] Both Mick and Ralph sell special items if the right circumstances are met. With at least 50 [[Speech (Fallout: New Vegas)|Speech]] or higher, both Mick and Ralph can be convinced to permit the use of these special services: * Mick's "special inventory" contains uncommon as well as a few rare [[Guns|ballistic]] weapons. He also sells the unique [[Naughty nightwear (Fallout: New Vegas)|naughty nightwear]]. * Ralph will sell a fake passport allowing for entry to the [[New Vegas Strip|Strip]] (if the 2000 [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|caps]] credit check cannot be met nor does one have 80 [[Science (Fallout: New Vegas)|Science]] to hack the greeter). It will cost 500 [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|caps]] to purchase or 375 with 50 [[Barter (Fallout: New Vegas)|Barter]], or it can be obtained for free if the favor from [[The King]] is used to request getting a passport (requires completing [[G.I. Blues]]). ==Notable loot== * [[Pimp-Boy 3 Billion]] - Given by Mick by completing [[How Little We Know]] in [[Omertas stopped buying from Mick|a certain way]] (see the quest's page for details). * 150 [[rocket souvenir]]s - In the [[Nuka-Cola vending machine (Fallout: New Vegas)|Nuka-Cola vending machine]] on the second floor. * [[Strange meat (Fallout: New Vegas)|Strange meat]] - Inside the fridges. * [[Container of chlorine]] - Purchased from Ralph. Relevant as a [[quest item]] during a certain part of How Little We Know. * [[Naughty nightwear (Fallout: New Vegas)|Naughty nightwear]] - Found inside the hidden storage room after passing Mick's Speech check to access his "special inventory." It must be stolen. * [[Embrace of the Mantis King! (GRA)|Embrace of the Mantis King!]] {{Icon|FNVGRA}} - Sold by Mick. * [[Nuka-Breaker (GRA)|Nuka-Breaker]] {{Icon|FNVGRA}} - Sold by Mick. * [[Li'l Devil (GRA)|Li'l Devil]] {{Icon|FNVGRA}} - Sold by Mick. ==Notes== ===''Fallout: New Vegas''=== ;Effects of player's actions * If the [[Mick & Ralph's crier]] near the central gate is shot by the player character or a [[Fallout: New Vegas companions|companion]], they will no longer be able to buy anything from either Mick or Ralph. They will say how they do not like the way they treat their friends and tell them to leave. * If the Courier has a ''Mixed'' or better (neutral) Freeside reputation, a [[local]] will approach the player character to say that [[Mick & Ralph's]] will offer them a discount. The discount is intended to be +5% higher per reputation level, from 10% off at ''Mixed'' to 30% off at ''Wild Child''. ** {{BugOut}} The discounts do not function correctly in [[Mick (Fallout: New Vegas)|Mick's]] or [[Ralph (Fallout: New Vegas)|Ralph's]] dialogue, so they will almost never actually be applied; in fact, this can even cause the Courier to be unable to trade with Mick and Ralph when at a neutral Freeside reputation.{{Ref|(Bug)}} * Talking to Ralph while [[Wang Dang Atomic Tango]] is active will have him speak unique dialogue such as "Pimpin' ain't easy, huh? Maybe I'd stop by if that place got some talent." * When confronting him during [[Debt Collector]] for [[Francine Garret]], [[Santiago (Fallout: New Vegas)|Santiago]] will claim using the code word "extravaganza" gets a discount from Ralph. However, asking Ralph about it reveals this is a lie, one that Santiago frequently uses. ;Trivia * The hidden room housing Mick's "special inventory" features, along with a [[Tri-beam laser rifle (Fallout: New Vegas)|tri-beam laser rifle]], three weapons from ''[[Fallout 3]]'': a [[Railway rifle (Fallout 3)|railway rifle]], two [[Infiltrator (The Pitt)|Infiltrator]]s, and a [[Chinese pistol (Fallout 3)|Chinese pistol]] on the high right. None of these weapons are sold by Mick, and the displayed items themselves are not actual weapons but non-interactive decorations. * A small number of items inside Mick's "special inventory" room are actual items: [[Cowboy hat (Fallout: New Vegas)|cowboy hats]], naughty nightwear, and the lone duffle bag in the room, which is empty. All of these items are close enough that they can be picked up by viewing the room with the third-person camera. * The sign outside the building appears to have originally only said "Ralph's," indicating the "Mick &" part was added post-War. * At the front desk where Ralph usually sits, hanging over it on the right side, are some dolls that the [[swampfolk]] of [[Point Lookout (location)|Point Lookout]] hung on trees to mark their territory. * Several [[Vault 3]] [[Vault jumpsuit (Fallout: New Vegas)|jumpsuits]] can be found in the upstairs section of the shop. They are also sold by Mick, though both sources have them in poor condition. * Similar to [[Rockopolis]] in ''Fallout 3'', the hidden area of the shop uses pennants to mark the location. * There are two posters for the [[Museum of Technology]] which advertise the [[Virgo II|Virgo II Lunar Lander]], which is seen on display in the museum in ''Fallout 3''. * When entering Mick and Ralph's, directly to the left, there are ads for the [[Super-Duper Mart (company)|Super-Duper Mart]] from ''Fallout 3''. * [[Dixon (Fallout: New Vegas)|Dixon]] will look through the windows of the shop even though they cannot be seen through. * If the player uses any means of continuing the game after the ending slideshow, Ralph will comment on the outcome of the [[Second Battle of Hoover Dam]]. ===''Fallout'' TV series=== * The location of Mick & Ralph's storefront differs in the ''Fallout'' TV series compared to ''Fallout: New Vegas''. In the game, the store is situated close to [[Freeside's east gate]], while in the show, it is one of the last buildings on the left before reaching [[The Strip North Gate]]. It is also shown as being directly across the street from the [[King's School of Impersonation]], which also changed position in the show compared to the game. ==Appearances== Mick & Ralph's appears only {{In|FNV}} and {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Bugs== * {{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} After convincing Mick to show you his "special" items, they will be available for the rest of the game as part of his "normal" sales items, but will not change. Further requests to browse his "special" inventory serve no purpose, other than to open the hidden door in the shop.{{Verify|verified}} * {{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} {{Note|(Bug)}} Mick and Ralph's intended ''Mixed'' reputation discounts fail to work, as the script conditions used to apply the discounts in their trading dialogue incorrectly use the function GetReputation instead of the function GetReputationThreshold. This causes the dialogue script to only give the discount if the Courier has '''Positive''' reputation rather than '''mixed''' reputation, and can actually make it so that Mick and Ralph are unable to trade with the player character when they have a mixed reputation (the dialogue will work, but the trading menu will not open).{{Verify|verified}} ** A solution is to change the player's Freeside reputation so that it's either positive or negative (by paying James Garret, completing quests, killing random people, or using the console on PC {for example "ResetAI"}) and then walk around the entrance of Mick & Ralph's (the area where [[Dixon]] walks; this area contains a script trigger block which updates variables related to the Courier's Freeside reputation), which will immediately fix the bug. * {{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} Occasionally, when you ask to see what either Mick or Ralph has in stock or for sale, no trade menu comes up and the conversation will end. The fix is if you have not yet completed the quest "Wang Dang Atomic Tango" given by James Garret in the Atomic Wrangler, complete this quest and sometimes this will allow you to be able to trade with Mick and Ralph again.{{Verify|verified}} ** This appears to be tied to Mick and Ralph's ''Mixed'' reputation discount bug; the same methods of changing Freeside reputation to positive or negative instead of neutral to fix the bug may apply here. * {{Platforms|ps3}} Ralph's [[Speech (Fallout: New Vegas)|Speech]] challenge for "special services" may not appear if you have completed all of [[The King]]'s quests.{{Verify|verified}} * {{Platforms|pc}} The "special weapons" area will not show up (obtained with Speech). You ask to see them and he waits but nothing happens (normal buy screen should appear but doesn't). It still works for normal guns, just not special weapons.{{Verify|verified}} * {{Platforms|pc,xbox360}} Having a high enough Freeside reputation causes a non-player character to praise you and give you various free items/caps occasionally. If one of these non-player characters approaches you while you're in Ralph's special item cell room Ralph may exit which can cause the room to seal with you in it. There appears to be no way out and you must reload from a saved game, or use the console to teleport yourself somewhere else.{{Verify|verified}} * {{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} Sometimes neither Mick nor Ralph will be present in the shop. There is no known fix to this bug.{{Verify|verified}} * {{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} Sometimes after being approached by a non-player character who gives you a discount at Mick & Ralph's, attempting to browse either of their stocks will simply send you back to the dialogue menu without displaying the items. After some testing, it appears to be caused by raising your Freeside fame to trigger the event, but also gaining Freeside infamy to the point of having a Mixed reputation before the non-player character has a chance to speak to you. You can avoid this bug via the use of console commands or simply by avoiding the non-player character running up to you in Freeside. Killing the non-player character will turn Mick & Ralph hostile the next time you enter their store, even if you were hidden.{{Verify|verified}} ==Gallery== MickRalphs interior.jpg|View at the store MickRalphs upstairs.jpg|Upstairs, 150 caps in the vending machine to the left Mick&Ralph's.jpg|Mick & Ralph's as seen during daylight SecretPlace.jpg|Mick's special store FNV Naughty nightwear Mick.jpg|[[Naughty nightwear (Fallout: New Vegas)|Naughty nightwear]] Workbench Mick and Ralphs.jpg|[[Workbench (Fallout: New Vegas)|Workbench]] Mick & Ralphs The Wrangler.png|[[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]] ("[[The Wrangler]]") {{Navbox Freeside}} {{Navbox New Vegas}} {{Navbox locations FNV}} [[Category:Freeside buildings]] [[Category:Fallout: New Vegas shops]] [[Category:Post-War businesses]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[de:Mick & Ralph's]] [[es:Mick & Ralph's]] [[it:Negozio di Mick e Ralph]] [[pt:Mick & Ralph's]] [[ru:Мик и Ральф]] [[uk:Мік та Ральф]]

{{Infobox location |games =FNV,FOTV |type =Building |image =The Kings.jpg |map marker image =King's School of Impersonation map.png |part of =[[Freeside]] |factions =[[Kings]] |leaders =[[The King]] |merchants =[[Sergio]] (barber) |robots =[[Rex (Fallout: New Vegas)|Rex]] |quests =[[G.I. Blues]]
[[Kings' Gambit]]
[[Nothin' But a Hound Dog]] |cell name =FreesideKingsHouse (interior) |refid ={{ID|10e03b}} (interior) }} {{Quotation|Oh, I know it says "school" out front, but everything in here seems to be related to the worship of [[Elvis Presley|some guy]] from back in the day.|[[The King]]|sound=FNV_TheKing_SchoolOutFront.ogg}} The '''King's School of Impersonation''' is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Freeside|unmarked location]] within [[Freeside]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], the building was host to an [[Elvis Presley]] impersonation school that served the greater Las Vegas area. It included the use of holotapes and outfits to teach how to mimic his voice and fashion as well as a classroom curriculum that taught how to replicate his speech patterns and catchphrases, and even what kind of foods he liked to eat.The [[Courier]]: ''"Is that what you guys do, pretend to be this guy?"''
The King: ''"Somethin' like that, yeah. There were some working tapes here when we first got here, so we know what he sounded like. Sadly, they stopped working a few years back, so I sold them to a junk merchant who was passing through, otherwise I'd play some for you. All the outfits you see my guy wearing around were originally found in here, too. Along with more hair gel than you can shake a stick at.
([[VFSTheKing.txt|The King's dialogue]]) Following the nuclear apocalypse, the building, like most of the area around Vegas was left to rot and ruin until [[Timeline#2274|2274]], when [[Robert House|Mr. House]] emerged from the [[Lucky 38]] with his [[Securitron]]s to establish [[New Vegas]] ahead of the arrival of the [[New California Republic]]. He issued an ultimatum to the [[tribals]] and raiders living in the ruins, ultimately recruiting those who became the [[Three Families]] while the rest were either evicted or killed. One of the tribal groups tried to eke out a living in the slums but found firsthand how rough living could be. They eventually came across the King's School of Impersonation and learned about the image and ideals of one called "the King" (they never learned his real name as all evidence had been unintelligbly degraded). Inspired, the tribals reinvented themselves as the [[Kings]], led by [[The King]], based around the anarchic ideal of complete personal freedom, where "every man is a king in [their] own right."The [[Courier]]: ''"Tell me about the Kings."''
The King: ''"We're different than other gangs, and not just because we dress better. We're not just a group of thugs looking for our next fight. The Kings are about an idea, you see? Where every man is free to follow his own path, do his own thing. Where every man is a king in his own right."''
([[VFSTheKing.txt|The King's dialogue]]) ==Layout== Situated southeast of the [[Atomic Wrangler Casino]] in the south section of Freeside, the building interior is sizable and consists of three floors. All items in the building are considered owned and in taking them, [[Karma (Fallout: New Vegas)|Karma]] will be lost. The sole exception are the beds which can be freely used to [[Resting|sleep]]. It can be entered through a door on the northmost corner of the building into a reception area. ===First floor=== In the reception room, couches line the wall, [[Empty whiskey bottle (Fallout: New Vegas)|empty whiskey bottle]]s litter the floor, and Kings gang members mill about the room, sitting on barstools around a semicircle countertop. An inoperable coffee machine sits on the counter and a broken freezer behind contains [[empty Sunset Sarsaparilla bottle]]s. There are two directions to proceed from the reception area. To the left of the counter is the entrance to a theater of sorts, with a stage, spotlights, and seating. [[Pacer]] will stop the Courier upon approach, requiring payment of 50 or 500 caps to speak with The King. The Courier can offer 5 caps, which he will refuse unless a 60 Speech check is passed, or pay no caps by passing the initial 60 Speech check. No matter what amount is given to Pacer, if the Courier tells The King, he will reimburse the player character and have unique comments on each differing sum. Inside the stage room, a Kings gang member performs for The King, who sits in front of the stage joined by his [[Cyberdog (Fallout: New Vegas)|cyberdog]], [[Rex (Fallout: New Vegas)|Rex]]. A locked door on the southside of the stage room can only be opened with [[The King's key]], obtainable only by pickpocketing. The area behind the door is accessible immediately by following the hallways of the first floor, and therefore pickpocketing the key is unnecessary to explore the building in full. The second way to proceed from the reception area is a door directly opposite the main entrance. It leads to the living areas of the building, of which there are three floors. Each floor contains bedrooms, recreation rooms, and storage areas. Rooms on the first floor include a storage closet full of wire music stands, and two bathrooms. There are three bedrooms containing nine total beds and two dressing rooms on the first floor. In one of the rooms, cups alongside three [[ping pong ball]]s are set up as if to play beer pong. In one of the dressing rooms, [[Sergio]] can be found. He is the gang's hairstylist. If the Courier becomes a member of the gang, they can change their hairstyle here. The staircase to the second floor is located in the west corner. ===Second floor=== The second floor has two bathrooms that are larger than those on the preceding floor. The lefthand bathroom has three stalls and two sinks, while the righthand stall has two stalls, two urinals, and one sink. All of the water in these bathrooms is radiation-free. In the righthand bathroom, a [[straight razor]] can be found on the edge of the sink with a pool of blood on the floor, presumably from a botched shaving attempt. A [[First aid box (Fallout: New Vegas)|first aid box]] is mounted on the wall in each bathroom. Apart from the bathrooms, this floor is comprised entirely of bedrooms. There are six bedrooms containing 21 beds on the second floor. The bedrooms have various personal effects within, including [[Switchblade (Fallout: New Vegas)|switchblades]], [[Cherry bomb (Fallout: New Vegas)|cherry bombs]], and alcohol bottles. One bedroom has a battery-powered light on the ground next to [[Scrap metal (Fallout: New Vegas)|scrap metal]], a [[Hammer (Fallout: New Vegas)|hammer]], and a [[Wrench (Fallout: New Vegas)|wrench]]. Another bedroom has a [[Chessboard (Fallout: New Vegas)|chessboard]] propped up on cinderblocks. A bedroom in the north corner has a mattress lying on a desk, with a bottle of [[Wine (Fallout: New Vegas)|wine]] balanced on top. The Kings have turned another bedroom into a putting green, lining up squares of carpet underneath a cup on its side, with four [[Golf ball (Fallout: New Vegas)|golf balls]] and a [[9 iron]]. The staircase to the third floor is located in the south corner of the building. ===Third floor=== By proceeding in a clockwise fashion, the Courier will first find Pacer's bedroom, with a lit cigar on the end table next to a queen-sized bed. This bed will grant the Courier the [[Well Rested]] effect, as will the other beds on the third floor. The next room is a storage room filled with desks. To the right of the storage room is the bedroom of The King. A Kings member stands guard outside. The bedroom is large, with windows extending to the top of the tall, coffered ceiling. Looking at the building from outside, the third-floor windows on the recessed walls above the main entrance belong to this room. The bedroom is occupied by two [[King groupie]]s wearing [[Sexy sleepwear (Fallout: New Vegas)|sexy sleepwear]]. They cannot be engaged in dialogue but will say various things about The King or ask if the Courier is supposed to be there. The room has a unique heart-shaped bed, a [[Fallout 3 and New Vegas miscellaneous world objects#Pool table|pool table]], [[Jukebox (Fallout: New Vegas)|jukebox]], and a [[Sunset Sarsaparilla vending machine (Fallout: New Vegas)|Sunset Sarsaparilla vending machine]]. The King can be found sitting in the chair next to the jukebox at times, next to Rex, behind a table with a ''[[Boxing Times]]'' skill magazine and [[Harmonica (Fallout: New Vegas)|harmonica]]. Connected to The King's bedroom is the bedroom belonging to the groupies, fitted with two queen-sized beds, a vanity, and a bathtub. The last room on the third floor is filled with clothing items, including [[Kings outfit]]s and [[Jailhouse Rocker (Fallout: New Vegas)|Jailhouse Rocker]]s. If the Courier joins the gang, they will be given an outfit of their own. There is a large chalkboard on the wall with faint writing. Upon closer inspection, the Courier can read a "King Impersonation Checklist" with instructions to "move hips," "say 'uh huh'," "say momma," and "peanut butter & banana sandwiches" as well as "This week's homework" including "(illegible) girls (illegible)," "gyrate," and "aint nothin but a hound dog" written across the bottom. Other chalkboards can be found throughout the building featuring similar scribbles, including "make $$$." The hallway leads back to the stairway in the south corner. ==Notable loot== * 32 [[Kings outfit]]s and three [[Jailhouse Rocker (Fallout: New Vegas)|Jailhouse Rocker]]s - On the third floor. * Three [[ping pong ball]]s - In a first-floor bedroom. * [[Figaro]] - a unique variant of the [[straight razor]], carried by [[Sergio]]. * [[Viva Las Vegas]] - Carried by [[The King]]. * Four [[Golf ball (Fallout: New Vegas)|golf balls]] - In a second-floor bedroom along with a [[9 iron]]. ==Related quests== * [[G.I. Blues]] * [[Kings' Gambit]] * [[Nothin' But a Hound Dog]] ==Notes== The location of the King's School of Impersonation differs in the ''Fallout'' TV series compared to ''Fallout: New Vegas''. In the game, the store is situated near the beginning of the south-central part of Freeside, while in the show, it is one of the last buildings on the right before reaching [[The Strip North Gate]]. It is also shown as being directly across the street from [[Mick & Ralph's]], which also changed position in the show compared to the game. ==Appearances== The King's School of Impersonation appears {{In|FNV}} and {{in|FOTV|noin}}. ==Behind the scenes== The in-game King's School of Impersonation is based on the real-world location of [[wikipedia:Four Queens|Four Queens Hotel and Casino]], located in the [[wikipedia:Fremont Street Experience|Fremont Street Experience]] in [[wikipedia:Las Vegas|Las Vegas, Nevada]]. Many aspects of the casino bear resemblance to the in-game equivalent, including the building's structure, name and design. ==Bugs== {{Platforms|pc,ps3,xbox360}} When playing as a female character, random members of the Kings will occasionally say the usual "Ever heard of personal space guy?" but if subtitles are turned on they will read "Ever heard of personal space lady?", other times the gang members will say "lady."{{verify|verified}} ==Gallery== ===''Fallout: New Vegas''=== Kings_SOI_reception.jpg|Reception Kings_SOI_bedroom.jpg|Prime bedroom, with one of the Kings' [[King groupie|groupies]] Kings_SOI_bedr2.jpg|Second bedroom Kings bathroom floor 2.png|Bathroom second floor Kings putting green floor 2.png|Improvised putting green Kings chalkboard 1.png|Small chalkboard Kings beer pong floor 1.png|Beer pong setup Kings heart bed floor 3.png|The King's unique heart-shaped bed Kings outfit room floor 3.png|Outfit room Kings chalkboard 2.png|"King Impersonation Checklist" Kings SOI stage.jpg|The stage room ====Art assets==== FNV Brian Menze concept art 14.jpg|Concept art by [[Brian Menze]] Kingssign lod.png|Sign texture file Kingschalkboardblank01.png|Texture file King'schalkboarddirty01.png|Texture file ===''Fallout'' TV series=== The Kings SOI 1 The Wrangler.png|[[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]] ("[[The Wrangler]]") The Kings SOI 2 The Wrangler.png|''Fallout'' TV series ("The Wrangler") ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Freeside}} {{Navbox New Vegas}} {{Navbox locations FNV}} [[Category:Freeside buildings]] [[Category:Kings]] [[Category:Pre-War companies]] [[Category:Pre-War educational institutions]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[de:Schule der Verkörperung des Kings]] [[es:Escuela del Fraude de los Reyes]] [[it:King's School of Impersonation]] [[pl:Szkoła Sobowtórów Króla]] [[ru:Школа двойников Короля]] [[uk:Школа двійників Короля]] [[zh:貓王的演藝學校]]

The Atomic Wrangler has you covered!|[[Atomic Wrangler crier]]|sound=NVAtomicWranglerCrierAtomicWranglerHasYouCovered.ogg}} The '''Atomic Wrangler Bar & Casino''', typically shortened to just the '''Atomic Wrangler''', is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Freeside|unmarked location]] within [[Freeside]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}.{{FOTV|2|5}} ==Background== {{Quotation|It's not much to look at, but if you can't afford to get into The Strip, the Atomic Wrangler's the best place to gamble in Freeside.|[[Fallout: New Vegas loading screens|''Fallout: New Vegas'' loading screen]]}} The Atomic Wrangler Bar & Casino was a pre-[[Great War|War]] nightclub located on [[Fremont Street]] in [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], advertising itself as "the West's finest watering hole."[[:File:AtomicWranglerAdv.png|Atomic Wrangler billboard]] In 2077, it played host to a meeting between [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] and [[Diane Welch|Congresswoman Diane Welch]], who arranged for Howard to secretly meet with the [[Last President of the United States|U.S. president]] in order to give him the [[Cold fusion|cold fusion diode]] Howard had stolen from [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]].{{FOTV|2|7}} By [[Timeline#2281|2281]], the Atomic Wrangler is the only active [[Fallout: New Vegas casinos|casino]] in the slum community of Freeside,[[:File:FNV Atomic Wrangler card.png|Vault playing card]] also doubling as a flophouse, brothel, and prominent source of the [[chems]] craze in the area. Its owners and operators are the Garret twins, [[James Garret|James]] and [[Francine Garret|Francine]], who keep a staff of armed thugs for protection and provide service even to members of the [[Van Graffs]] in the nearby [[Silver Rush]] and the [[Kings]] from the down-the-street [[King's School of Impersonation]]. Many caravaneers and poor (but not impoverished) [[New California Republic|NCR]] folks can also be found here when they lack deep enough pockets to make it to the [[New Vegas Strip|Strip]].[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland#2C.06 Atomic Wrangler Casino|''Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition'' Tour of the Mojave Wasteland; 2C.06 Atomic Wrangler Casino]] As of 2296, the Atomic Wrangler continues to operate in Freeside, though by then, the barkeep is a man named [[Shotgun Jeff]] and it is unclear whether the Garret twins are still involved with the establishment. ==Layout== ===''Fallout: New Vegas''=== Situated in the south end of Freeside, the Wrangler can be seen past the patched-together "Freeside" sign on the west side with itself featuring a neon sign of a futuristic cowboy riding a stylized atom. ====Bottom level==== The main room has a vaulted ceiling, a stage, and a bar. The room directly opposite the entrance features the casino's [[Atomic Wrangler cashier|cashier]] and casino games. The cashier's room contains some [[Pre-War money (Fallout: New Vegas)|pre-War money]] and [[Fallout: New Vegas consumables|chems]] in the safes. To the right are the bathrooms and a staircase to the second story balconies. Behind the bar is a kitchen and storeroom, accessible via a door around the corner near the bathroom with a Very Hard lock. Both of the Garrets have the [[Fallout: New Vegas keys#Atomic Wrangler upstairs key|key]] to the room, but it will eventually become unlocked as soon as one of the Garrets head upstairs to their room, as they neglect to relock it. The storage room/kitchen area behind the bar contains a significant amount of common items of moderate value, such as various alcoholic beverages. The Courier can also find a large number of [[Fresh apple (Fallout: New Vegas)|fresh apples]], [[Fresh pear (Fallout: New Vegas)|pears]], and [[Fresh carrot (Fallout: New Vegas)|carrots]] (at least a half-dozen each), as well as a weapons locker and medicine locker, both containing many useful items. ====Second level==== This level has a balcony that oversees the stage and bar. Off of the balcony are four rooms. A rentable room is located in the eastern corner of the second floor. Stairways lead back down or up to the third level. ====Corner room==== {{main|Atomic Wrangler corner room}} On the second level, there is a door that leads to the corner room, which can be gained as [[Fallout: New Vegas player character housing|player housing]] after completing [[Debt Collector]] for Francine. ====Third level==== This level is where the employees, including the Garret twins, live. In the employee living area, four guards can be found either milling around or sleeping. The door to this level is secured with an Average lock or opened with the key held by the Garrets. Guards here will not be hostile initially, instead following the Courier around, repeating a warning to leave. Rooms include a large bedroom the Garret twins take turns sleeping in, two general sleeping areas for employees (one containing 8 beds and one with 6 beds), two bathrooms and a storage room. Guard sleeping areas have [[Footlocker (Fallout: New Vegas)|footlockers]] with minor loot. The two bathrooms contain [[First aid box (Fallout: New Vegas)|first aid box]]es. The storage room, located to the right of the sleeping area, is filled with file cabinets, metal crates, and a gun cabinet. ===''Fallout'' TV series=== The Atomic Wrangler, as depicted in the TV series, has both similarities to and differences from its portrayal in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. The casino storefront is still located across from the [[Silver Rush]], except down at the end of a main street with multiple other stores including [[Sonny's Sundries]]. The bottom floor is widely different from its previous appearance, with glass double doors instead of one door, no visible evidence of a performance stage, and the second floor balcony extending above the bar. The staircase itself is also relocated into a curved form opposite from the bar instead of behind it. What's shown of the upper floors consists mostly of a single hotel room which has an attached bathroom and open windows looking out into Freeside. ==Gambling== [[File:TheAtomicWrangler.jpg|thumb|220px|The gambling tables]] ; Games * The Atomic Wrangler offers [[Blackjack]], [[Roulette]], and [[Slots]]. * The Atomic Wrangler pays 6:5 on blackjack, and the dealer must draw to 16. ; Rewards and Ban As the player earns chips, the casino offers increasingly valuable gifts: * 1,250+ chips: [[Beer (Fallout: New Vegas)|beer]] * 2,500+ chips: [[Whiskey (Fallout: New Vegas)|whiskey]] and dapper gambler hat * 3,750+ chips: [[absinthe]], [[Rum & Nuka]] & [[dapper gambler suit]] * 5000+ chips: banned from gambling. After the player character earns 5,000+ chips, they will be banned from playing games in the Atomic Wrangler Casino. They can still use its other functions, such as the bar and services of the prostitutes (if [[Wang Dang Atomic Tango]] has been completed), but they cannot win any more money, permanently. If the player character breaks the house limit before getting any comp gifts (by getting a large win) they will not receive any comps they have missed. There is no floor manager at this casino, so the comp gifts are awarded directly to the player character upon reaching each winning milestone. Play is still interrupted by the player character being forced out of whichever game they were playing to receive the message rewarding their earned comps. ==Inhabitants== * [[Atomic Wrangler cashier]] * [[Atomic Wrangler guard]] * [[Caleb McCaffery]] (before completing Debt Collector) * [[Francine Garret]] * [[Hadrian (Fallout: New Vegas)|Hadrian]] (before completing Talent Pool) * [[Henry Jamison]] * [[James Garret]] * [[Beatrix Russell]] (after completing Wang Dang Atomic Tango) * [[Fisto (character)|Fisto]] (after completing Wang Dang Atomic Tango) * [[Santiago (Fallout: New Vegas)|Santiago]] or [[Old Ben]] (after completing Wang Dang Atomic Tango) ==Notable loot== * [[Nuka-Cola Victory (Fallout: New Vegas)|Nuka-Cola Victory]] - On the third level in the Garrets' room, on a shelf. ==Related quests== {{columns|2| * [[Debt Collector]] * [[Talent Pool]] * [[Wang Dang Atomic Tango]] * ''[[Big Winner, Atomic Wrangler]]'' * ''[[Friend of the Followers]]'' * ''[[Long-Term Care]]'' * ''[[Smooth-Talking Criminal]]'' }} ==Notes== * The casino's [[Atomic Wrangler crier|crier]] can be found outside on the street corner below the "Freeside" sign, advertising the casino to the public. * Despite the Wrangler's reputation as a free-swinging brothel, dialogue options with Francine Garret that would suggest the same, and sex noises coming through the walls of most rooms, there are no prostitutes in the casino beyond ones the player character recruits during Wang Dang Atomic Tango. After finishing the quest, one can then have sex with either ghoul cowgirl/dominatrix Beatrix Russell, Santiago/Old Ben (depending on decisions during the quest), or the sex-bot Fisto. * Like all other casinos in the game, the amount of money kept in the cashier's office is small. Robbing the cashier nets at random a few dozen bundles of pre-War money and approximately 100 [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|caps]]. The [[Fallout: New Vegas keys#Atomic Wrangler bank key|Atomic Wrangler bank key]] is carried by both Garret twins. * Exiting from dialogue with Fisto will give 10 [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|caps]], which can be repeated ad infinitum. * Being banned from the casino by gambling does not affect the progress of completing the [[The Courier Who Broke the Bank]] achievement/trophy. * The casino also appears in ''[[Fallout 76]]'' as a [[Fallout 76 shelters|shelter]] purchasable in the [[Atomic Shop]]. In-game it has a similar layout to its initial appearance though is larger than it appeared in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. ==Behind the scenes== ;''Fallout: New Vegas'' * The in-game Atomic Wrangler Casino is based on the real-world Atomic Liquors store, located on [[wikipedia:Fremont Street|Fremont Street]] in downtown Las Vegas. * The logo of the Atomic Wrangler is a reference to a scene in the film ''[[Wikipedia:Dr. Strangelove|Dr. Strangelove]]'' in which Major T. J. "King" Kong rides a falling nuclear bomb like a rodeo cowboy. * Area designer [[Robert Lee]], who was one of three designers on Freeside, wrote for characters within this location and designed the quests [[Wang Dang Atomic Tango]] and [[Debt Collector]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E4zN5Qy3Izo Freeside's Cut Content] ;''Fallout'' TV series * In season 2 of the TV series, Freeside and the exterior of the Atomic Wrangler were filmed at [[wikipedia:Movie ranch#Monogram Ranch/Melody Ranch|Melody Ranch Motion Picture Studio]] in [[wikipedia:Santa Clarita, California|Santa Clarita, California]]. Melody Ranch has previously been used to film prominent Westerns as well as TV series like ''[[wikipedia:Westworld (TV series)|Westworld]]'', also produced by [[Jonathan Nolan]] and [[Lisa Joy]].[https://archive.ph/HTk7h Los Angeles Times: "‘Fallout’ fans know New Vegas. How the show brought the video game location to life"][[:File:FOTV season 2 Johnny Pemberton Freeside tour.mp4|Freeside film set behind-the-scenes tour]] by [[Johnny Pemberton]] {{Quotation|The Atomic Wrangler was so specific in the game. It has specific architecture and has this terrific neon sign that I love with the cowboy ... There's no way to take [a building that] already existed [on set] and have it look like the Atomic Wrangler ... so I put a facade in front of a facade.|[[Howard Cummings]], quoted by the L.A. Times}} * The interior of the Atomic Wrangler was also shot at Melody Ranch, but in a different building across the street from the one used for the exterior. The building used for the interior was the one used to film the [[w:c:westworld:Mariposa Saloon|Mariposa Saloon]] in ''Westworld'', with some features such as the stage moved to a different side. ==Bugs== {| class="va-table va-table-full mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" ! colspan="1" | Bugs |- | * {{Platforms|ps3}} Once a player attempts to go to the second floor, or perhaps attempts to lockpick the offices/rooms, a bug may occur that interferes with interactions with non-player characters inside of the Atomic Wrangler.
